title: Mars and Jupiter Are About to Meet in the Sky
summary:
Look up on the night of November 15-16, and you will see two planets putting on a show. Mars and Jupiter will look very close together in the stars called Leo. They will not be this close again until July 2029.

The two planets will rise in the east around midnight. Mars will shine red, and Jupiter will shine bright next to it. The blue-white star Regulus will glow below them.

It is a trick of how we see things. Mars and Jupiter are really more than 368 million miles apart. They only look close because they line up from Earth.

Astronomers call this meeting an appulse. It happens about once every two to two and a half years, when Mars catches up to Jupiter.

Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets." That means they orbit farther from the sun than Earth does. Through a telescope, they always look full and round.

A six-inch telescope shows how different the two worlds are. Jupiter has giant bands of cloud. Mars looks red, with dark patches of rock.
why_it_matters: You can step outside on a clear night and see two planets with your own eyes, which makes the solar system feel real and close.
